title: Matched thalamic recordings assign most of the estimated passive burst-fraction change to burst starts, with an uncertain total change
abstract: We separated burst starts per spike from spikes per burst in the same IBL thalamic units during task and passive spontaneous epochs. The sample had 8,547 units in 27 nuclei and 89 mice. In 87 mice with burst events in both epochs, the mean burst-fraction change was +0.585 percentage points, with a whole-mouse 95 percent interval of -0.103 to +1.471. A symmetric product identity assigned +0.567 points to starts and +0.018 points to size. Mean size changed by +0.023 spikes per burst, with interval -0.025 to +0.075. Across all 89 mice, events per unit-second increased by 0.01575, with interval 0.00246 to 0.03116. Lab deletion and sampling weights changed the total burst-fraction estimate. The estimated contrast mainly reflected starts, but its total remained uncertain. Rounded source summaries, unequal epoch lengths, unit selection and absent state-specific shuffles limit interpretation. No calcium, wiring or cell-type mechanism is identified. Code, licensed source tables, exact hashes, aggregate evidence and a static figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Matched-epoch change, product allocation and nucleus values. Bars show equal-mouse means and marginal whole-mouse bootstrap intervals.
